feature: A copy follows the original's look
summary: Changing a component's fade, blur, rounded corners, border or shadow now reaches every copy you have placed, part by part. A copy you styled yourself keeps what you set, says which parts are its own, and has a way back to following the original.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Components and the Library are on by default.

try.do: Draw a rectangle and a line of text over it, select both and press Command G.
Press Option Command K to make it a component, name it Setting, then drop two copies of it out of the Library onto empty canvas.
Select the ORIGINAL and drag Corner Radius up in Effects, then switch Enable Shadow on.
Select ONE copy and drag its Opacity down to about a third.
Select the original again and give it a Border of a few points.
Select the original and drag its Opacity to about three quarters.
Select the copy you faded and look at its Component section and its Effects section.
Click the back arrow beside Opacity in Effects to put that copy on the original's look again.

evaluate: When you rounded the original, did the copies changing feel like the app doing what you meant, or like something moving behind your back?
The faded copy took the original's new border but kept its own fade. Is that what you expected, or would you rather one edit to a copy took its whole look off the original?
Did you notice the back arrow beside Opacity, or did you have to go looking for a way to undo it?
Is 'Its own look: Opacity' on the copy's section worth the row, or is the arrow in Effects enough on its own?
The pill counted one copy when only one followed the fade. Does that number tell you what you want to know?
rough: The original's section says how many copies follow it but not which of them have looks of their own, so finding the odd copy out means clicking through them.
The shadow's way back sits on the Enable Shadow row, not on the shadow control you actually touched. A shadow is one thing here, so six identical arrows felt worse than one that is a row or two away.
Nothing warns you the moment you drag a slider on a copy that this part has stopped following. It shows afterwards, as an arrow you can press.
A copy's size, place, name and hidden state still do not follow the original, which is deliberate: those are what let copies sit in different spots.
Screen Recording was granted for this run, so both pictures are the real window, taken by Scripts/playtest/component-look-walk.json.
